findings.evidence: `rg` finds only `conjugate_one` at line 208 and `conjugate_conjugate` at line 214; the adapter definitions at lines 271, 291, 302, 349, 357, and 424 have no `_one` or composition theorem. Parallel layer APIs expose `LayerRefinement.galHom_trans`, `cohomologyInfl_trans`, and `tateInfl_trans`, and `LayerRestriction.galHom_trans` and `cohomologyRes_trans`.
findings.fix: Add identity and composition theorems (with the necessary transport along `conjugate_one`/`conjugate_conjugate`) for the group and coefficient equivalences and derive matching laws for `conjugateCohomologyIso` and `conjugateTateIso`; include the norm-quotient equivalence if it is part of the canonical adapter API.
findings.issue: Only the layers themselves satisfy `conjugate_one` and `conjugate_conjugate`; no corresponding laws characterize `conjugateGalEquiv`, the coefficient/ground-level equivalences, or the induced ordinary/Tate cohomology maps. Consumers therefore cannot rewrite iterated conjugation without unfolding implementations.

summary: The conjugation adapters lack the identity and composition laws needed to expose the claimed group action as a usable canonical API.
